title: Evidence Added where the Inspection Clock of a Keyturn Vehicle Listing Has Run Long
content:
Where a Keyturn Vehicle Listing has gone a long time since its last completed inspection, the marketplace files more photographs with a fault report, and how many more turns on how much of the inspection interval the vehicle has left.

1. A vehicle whose last completed inspection is more than 180 calendar days before the handling date and which has fewer than 2000 miles of inspection interval left adds 3 photographs.

2. A vehicle more than 180 calendar days past its last completed inspection with 2000 miles or more of interval left adds 2 photographs.

3. Any other vehicle adds nothing on this ground, an addition of 0 photographs.

### Where each boundary falls

*The day count.* Both of the first two clauses need the last completed inspection to be **more than** 180 calendar days before the handling date. A vehicle inspected exactly 180 calendar days before the handling date is on neither, and adds 0 photographs whatever its interval shows; a vehicle inspected 181 calendar days before it is on one of the two.

*The interval left.* Where the day count is met, the split is at 2000 miles of interval left: 1999 miles left is fewer than 2000 and adds 3 photographs; 2000 miles left exactly is 2000 miles or more and adds 2 photographs.

| Last completed inspection | Interval left | Added |
| --- | --- | --- |
| more than 180 calendar days back | fewer than 2000 miles | 3 photographs |
| more than 180 calendar days back | 2000 miles or more | 2 photographs |
| 180 calendar days back or less | any | 0 photographs |
